title: A Stability Framework for Parameter Selection in the Minimum Covariance Determinant Problem
summary: The paper addresses selection of the MCD subset size h, equivalently the number of outliers, which is usually chosen by arbitrary rules. It proposes a depth-initialized best-subset MCD algorithm without reweighting, a bootstrap clustering-instability estimator, and an integrated instability metric that adds a normalized log-Wasserstein correction to handle masking. On real data it selects h = 40 for StarsCYG with 7 outliers, h = 84 for banknotes with 16 outliers, and sensible (q, h) settings for fruit, glass, and breast-cancer examples, with simulations supporting the metric.

match_target.why: StarsCYG is tiny (n=47, p=2), the paper reports a 3-second grid search, and h=40 with 7 outliers is the paper's headline real-data demonstration of the integrated instability metric.

tolerance.why: No repeated-run standard deviation is reported. Rule 4 (10% relative) applied to the implied 7-outlier count gives 0.7, rounded up to integer precision; allowance is +/- 1 on the selected h or outlier count for this discrete target pair (h=40, 7 outliers).

requirements.stmt: Compute projection depths using the hybrid direction scheme: the first 500 data-driven directions, remaining uniform on the unit sphere; total max{1000, 100p}.
requirements.quote: the first 500 directions are generated using the data-driven method, while the remaining directions are sampled uniformly from the unit sphere.

requirements.stmt: Initialize H as the h observations with largest projection depths, then repeatedly apply C-steps until the subset stabilizes.
requirements.quote: Update H using concentration steps (1), (2), and (3) until H stabilizes.

requirements.stmt: Do not apply reweighting in the Depth-MCD best-subset algorithm.
requirements.quote: so we choose to omit reweighting in our subset selection algorithm.

requirements.stmt: For each bootstrap pair, apply Depth-MCD to both bootstrap samples and reuse original-sample projection depths for all h.
requirements.quote: we set the depths of observations within a bootstrapped sample to be their computed depth in the original sample.

requirements.stmt: For each bootstrap pair, compute Mahalanobis distances of the original n observations using the bootstrap subset estimates and define psi=1 outside the h-largest distances.
Use the scaled clustering distance p^c = p/c with c = 2(h/n)((n-h)/n), and average log(1 + p^c) over B independent bootstrap pairs.
Compute the squared Wasserstein distance between bootstrap normal estimates using equation (11), apply log(1 + W2), and average over bootstrap pairs.
requirements.quote: To stabilize the variance of the Wasserstein distances, we apply a log(1 + x) transformation.

requirements.stmt: Form the integrated instability metric I(h) = (1-beta)s(h) + beta(w(h)-min_l w(l)), with beta chosen so the standard deviation of (1-beta)s is lambda=3 times that of beta(w-min w).
requirements.quote: Based on empirical evidence, we consistently use lambda = 3 throughout the paper, as it performs well across a wide range of scenarios.

requirements.stmt: Select h by minimizing the integrated instability metric over the search grid; for StarsCYG use all h in {25,...,46} with 100 bootstrap pairs and exclude h=47.
requirements.quote: The grid search takes 3 seconds to complete, applying Algorithm 2 with 100 bootstrap pairs.

requirements.stmt: For ROBPCA extension, perform PcaHubert with alpha=0.5 on each bootstrap sample, apply Depth-MCD to robust principal component scores, and select (q,h) minimizing instability.
requirements.quote: we leverage the PcaHubert function (Hubert et al., 2005) from the R package rrcov with alpha = 0.5.

requirements.stmt: Use the MCD covariance determinant and Mahalanobis distance definitions from equations (1)-(2); each C-step must decrease the determinant monotonically.
requirements.quote: Rousseeuw and Driessen (1999) showed that each C-step monotonically decreases det(Sigma-hat).

data.name: StarsCYG
data.how_to_get: Use starsCYG from the R package robustbase, or the copy in the StableMCD GitHub repository; n=47, p=2 log light/temperature.

data.name: Swiss banknote data
data.how_to_get: Use the Flury (1988) banknote data, available via the StableMCD GitHub repository; n=100, p=6.

data.name: Fruit spectra data
data.how_to_get: Use the cantaloupe cultivar spectra data from Hubert and Van Driessen (2004), available via the StableMCD GitHub repository; n=1096, p=256.

data.name: Glass EPXMA spectra
data.how_to_get: Use the glass EPXMA data from Lemberge et al. (2000), available via the StableMCD GitHub repository; n=180, p=750.

data.name: TCGA-BRCA mRNA expression
data.how_to_get: Download TCGA-BRCA mRNA expression and ER status from cBioPortal at https://www.cbioportal.org/; apply log2(x+1), retain top 2,000 variable genes, and use the 1,050 ER-positive/negative samples.

data.name: Simulated settings 1-8
data.how_to_get: Generate from the protocols in Sections 4.1 and 4.2; no external data files are needed.
